card.name: Sasa
card.tagline: Samoa's seated group dance — rows of dancers slapping bodies, thighs, and ground in unison, faster and faster until the climax.
card.profile: Sasa, also spelled sāsā, is a type of folk dance from Samoa. Sasa is performed by all ages and genders, usually in groups and while seated. The word "sāsā" literally means "to strike", and is characterized by precise, rhythmic claps and intricate hand movements.
card.insight: A dance by the name of sasa is first mentioned in the academic literature in Buck's field notes from 1927-28, but his descriptions more closely resemble a different Samoan dance, usually referred to as siva lapalapa.
